races.name: Racing To School Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Moriarty Moon
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator with four runs in similar Good-ground conditions going 3/4 for course suitability, the Michael Bell yard has a respectable 14-day strike rate and Jason Hart rides — 43 days off the track is worth monitoring though no obvious fitness concern at 2yo level.
runners_data.comment: Moriarty Moon has run over today's trip and going, carries a workable 135 lb from stall two, and his speed rating of 70 edges above his official mark — enough to make him a genuine threat; the concern is a winless recent spell across his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Mick's The Boy
runners_data.note: Front-runner by style who has run four times on Good ground and placed once, Billy Garritty knows this horse well and the Easterby yard fires plenty of runners; this 6f trip suits better than the 5f starts, though a 0W record from 8 runs is a clear caveat.
runners_data.comment: Mick's The Boy shaped with promise when second three starts back, and he arrives here with distance and going experience to call on, a 31-day break leaving him fresh off stall eight carrying 134 lb; the risk is that he has been winless in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Aura Of Melania
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's filly has the standout recent form in the race with multiple placed efforts at 6f-7f on Good, and Kevin Stott is a strong northern jockey booking — however she is a genuine hold-up type who will likely find herself unable to settle as far back as she needs in a pace-heavy field, which compromises her chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Aura Of Melania nonetheless brings solid recent placed efforts — second last time out and third two starts back — alongside experience of today's trip and going, though a mark of 63 and a mid-field ranking of fifth suggest she faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Spectacular Diver
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up juvenile is 5/5 in similar going and has placed twice at 5f on Good, though this 6f trip is a step up from all five previous starts and whether she truly sees out the extra furlong on a flat track is the key question for Sean Kirrane to manage.
runners_data.comment: Spectacular Diver showed plenty when finishing third one start back, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call on from stall five carrying 133 lb; the concern is that he has been winless in his last five starts and must bounce back from a seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Cheeky Chesca
runners_data.note: Front-running type who wears blinkers and has placed three times from ten starts, David Allan has strong course knowledge and the Easterby handler is in excellent form over 14 days — a poor recent Going record of 8/10 runs on Good without a win is a concern, however the blinkers may sharpen her focus at the start.
runners_data.comment: Cheeky Chesca arrives here in sharp order just nine days after her latest start, and back-to-back thirds in her two most recent outings show she is consistently finding the frame; winless in her last six, she remains the one to beat on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Lady Titania
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly has only three runs to her name, all on Soft or Good-to-Soft, making this Good surface an unknown quantity; a genuine closer by style who has been bumped to midfield on the map, her 3-run form string of 7-7-5 gives little confidence she can take the step up in competition here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, with back-to-back sevenths before a fifth latest, Lady Titania is hard to fancy on these figures, though a sharp trainer strike-rate and experience over today's trip offer slim crumbs of comfort from stall one.

runners_data.name: Johns Power
runners_data.note: Roger Fell's gelding has been running every few days (6 days since last run) with a form string including a 0 which suggests a non-completion or unseating, and has no winning or placing evidence on standard Good ground — a true closer who cannot access his natural rear position in this field, he looks exposed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked sixth of eight on our ratings, Johns Power faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a return to this surface six days ago keeps him fit and fresh.

runners_data.name: Steamy Wonder
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's filly has all three runs on Tapeta (Standard) and therefore this Good turf surface is completely untested — PJ McDonald is a quality booking but the move from artificial to turf is a significant unknown, and her natural hold-up style will be difficult to deploy with the pace map already crowded.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked towards the foot of our assessments, Steamy Wonder faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip before and a third one start back offers a slim crumb of encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Mick's The Boy and Cheeky Chesca are the two confirmed front-runners in this 8-runner 6f nursery, and both are likely to push for the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, unchallenged pace. On Good ground at Catterick over 6f, that kind of honest pace from the front typically stretches the field out early and sets up a strong-finishing run to the line, favouring horses who can sit just off the speed or come from midfield as the leaders tire. Aura Of Melania, Lady Titania, Johns Power, and Steamy Wonder are all true hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map purely because the field cannot accommodate that many closers at the rear — in reality, the pace bias here strongly benefits those who can travel prominently off the speed rather than genuine hold-up horses forced to wait. This race shape favours prominent-to-midfield runners who can track the pace war between the two leaders and capitalise as the front two inevitably come back to them in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy and Cheeky Chesca contest the lead hard, burning each other off in the first half.
scenarios.body: The sustained duel saps the front two's reserves, and horses tracking in third or fourth are perfectly placed to sweep through as the pace collapses inside the final furlong on Good ground at Catterick. Spectacular Diver and Moriarty Moon, both proven in similar going, are the profiles best placed to pick up the pieces from a driving finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mick's Boy Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mick's The Boy breaks cleanly and establishes a clear lead, forcing Cheeky Chesca to concede the front.
scenarios.body: With Mick's The Boy dictating a controlled gallop rather than a frenetic duel, the pace becomes more honest than brutal and the leader retains enough fuel to hold on — Billy Garritty's experience in these nurseries is a significant positive. Cheeky Chesca's record shows ability to place third or better even when not leading, and remains the most likely runner-up from the prominent group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel is truly extreme and the whole field gets strung out, allowing the furthest back runners to pick off the fading leaders.
scenarios.body: Aura Of Melania has the best recent form in the field with multiple placed efforts in similar conditions and would theoretically benefit from a thorough test — but she and Lady Titania are genuine hold-up types forced into midfield map positions, meaning this scenario relies on horses not getting their preferred berth. Even in a true pace meltdown, Moriarty Moon's proven Good-ground form over 6f gives it the best realistic chance of reaching the leaders in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two leaders is allowed to slip the field uncontested while the other fails to go with them early.
scenarios.body: This only materialises if Cheeky Chesca or Mick's The Boy is particularly slow from the gates and the other steals an unchallenged lead, which seems unlikely given both handlers will want pace. David Allan on Cheeky Chesca or Billy Garritty on Mick's The Boy would need an unusually clean break to replicate a wire-to-wire success, but the headgear angle on Cheeky Chesca (blinkers) slightly elevates this possibility.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Cheeky Chesca and Mick's The Boy both fly from the gates — if both attack the lead immediately, the ensuing duel could be truly punishing and collapse the form of both front-runners by the 2f pole.

Aura Of Melania's redistribution to midfield masks her true hold-up profile — if Kevin Stott attempts to push her forward into a more prominent position to compensate, she may expend too much early energy and fail to reproduce her recent placed form.

Spectacular Diver has run exclusively over 5f across five starts and steps up two furlongs here — if she lacks the stamina to sustain her run over the extra ground at Catterick, her Good-ground form figures become misleading.

Steamy Wonder has never raced on turf and switches from an artificial surface for the first time — monitor early market moves and paddock behaviour as any Going concern would significantly alter her profile for this shape.

Johns Power has run six days ago and the form figure "0" in his recent string needs clarification — if that represents a non-completion rather than a last-place finish, his physical readiness for another competitive effort so quickly should be treated with caution.

races.name: Racing Tv Club Day Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Apex Star
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with Good-ground placed form (2nd at 6f Good most recently relevant), has run well for Jason Hart before and the 19-day turnaround is fine; William Knight's 4/12 T14 strike rate is respectable and this is the horse's optimum trip and going.

runners_data.name: Persian Gate
runners_data.note: Headgear noted (p — first-time hood or similar), which adds an unknown element; finished 3rd on soft and 5th on standard, so Good ground is untested and the step into this company from a modest form base means reliance on the headgear spark.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prolific operation sends this horse back after 38 days — noteworthy freshness angle — and it has sound Good-ground placed form; its natural style is to come from well off the pace, but the small, slowly-run field means it will likely be ridden closer to the action than David Allan would ideally prefer.

runners_data.name: Khanimambo
runners_data.note: Two runs both on Good ground with modest finishing positions (6th and 7th), so no placed form to speak of; as a genuine hold-up operator pushed into a midfield slot by the race shape, it faces an uphill task unless the pace collapses and a sprint develops — David Nolan will need to be creative tactically.

runners_data.name: Triple P
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, and the only horse that will get its natural position uncontested; Duran Fentiman can dictate terms at a manageable tempo, and the Easterby yard is in strong form (T14: 14/87), though only two runs of form (3rd and 4th) makes its raw ability uncertain relative to rivals.

runners_data.name: Miss Veronika
runners_data.note: A 4-year-old whose form includes wide-margin positions over non-standard trips (17f soft, 16f good) alongside sprint efforts — a deeply inconsistent and puzzling profile; Harry Russell takes over for Brian Ellison (1/29 T14), and Good ground is only 1 from 4 in her history, making her hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a significant booking upgrade and gives this horse a significant tactical edge; three placed efforts on Good ground from five similar-ground runs and consistent proximity to the pace make Queen Sana well-suited to the anticipated race shape, though all wins have come over 5f and the 6f trip is at the outer edge of her comfort zone.

races.paceDynamic: Triple P is the one confirmed front-runner and, with just seven runners and no genuine rival to push them, Duran Fentiman can dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front on the Easterby runner. Apex Star and Queen Sana will press forward into prominent positions just off the pace, creating a race likely to be run at a sustainable, honest tempo rather than a lung-bursting sprint — conditions that suit horses who can travel close to the action and quicken in the straight. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural rear positions: Khanimambo, Stoneacre Joe, and Miss Veronika are true come-from-behind horses, but with the pace modest and only seven runners, at least some of them will be forced to travel closer to the pace than they would ideally like. This race shape — a steady-to-honest pace set by one controlled front-runner — decisively favours prominent racers and hold-up horses with enough finishing pace to close ground in the final two furlongs at Catterick's testing finish, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the most advantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Triple P dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent horses travel comfortably into the straight with cover.
scenarios.body: Triple P sets a sustainable pace that sees the race develop into a tactical sprint from the two-furlong pole, favouring those who have tracked the leader with minimal effort; Apex Star and Queen Sana, both prominent types with Good-ground form, are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Rush
scenarios.trigger: If Triple P goes too steady and the race becomes a sprint finish that catches front-runners flat-footed in the last furlong.
scenarios.body: A dawdling early pace compresses the field and the final two furlongs become a dash where late momentum can carry horses through; Stoneacre Joe and Khanimambo, if they can overcome the positional compromise of being pushed forward, could benefit from a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Triple P quickens the tempo from halfway and converts the solo lead into a wire-to-wire success on good ground.
scenarios.body: With no sustained pressure on the front, Triple P can find a rhythm that is hard to disrupt in a small field; the lack of a genuine pace challenger means the leader's energy reserves are intact for the crucial Catterick climb.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unusually strong pace develops and the field strings out, enabling genuine closers to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on horses like Khanimambo and Miss Veronika racing in something close to their true hold-up style, which the pace map suggests is unlikely given the limited field size; Persian Gate, with headgear noted and fresh, is the one with credentials if the race truly plays into staying-on hands.

watchPoints.text: Watch Triple P's early tempo — if Fentiman produces a very slow early gallop the race will compress and front-runners lose their edge, handing the finish to hold-up types who wouldn't normally get there.

Khanimambo and Stoneacre Joe are both genuine hold-up horses effectively forced forward by the race shape; if either is ridden against their nature and ties up in the final furlong, they could cause interference in a tight finish.
Queen Sana has all her placed form at 5f — if the 6f trip proves beyond her in the final stages despite a promising tactical position, she will empty quickly on Catterick's rising finish.

Persian Gate runs with headgear noted (p) which could alter its early behaviour significantly — monitor how it settles in the early stages, as a fizzy or free-going display would change the pace dynamic entirely.

Tim Easterby has two runners (Triple P and Stoneacre Joe) — watch for any market moves that indicate which horse the yard considers their main chance, as that could signal intended tactics from the front or behind.

races.name: Fifth Regiment Royal Artillery Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Daytona Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with 12-day turnaround for Ruth Carr, who fires runners fresh; has two placed efforts on Good going from 15 runs in similar conditions but no wins there, and pace-on bias in this race leaves her deeply disadvantaged from her natural rear position.
runners_data.comment: Daytona Lady arrives here just 12 days after finishing second two starts back, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions; our ratings just about make her the pick, though the trainer is in a lean spell and she is yet to win in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Giant
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good most recently, form that stands out in this field; holds up for Clifford Lee but needs a genuine closer's race to materialise, which this single front-runner shape is unlikely to provide cleanly — three Good-ground placed efforts in last five give him credentials if the race falls apart.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, making Giant a serious player here off a manageable 63 official mark; the chief concern is his trainer's deeply poor recent strike rate of just 4%.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: The lone pace-setter, wearing visor, who owns strong Good-going form including two wins from 11 runs on similar ground; Connor Beasley is a key booking and she is effectively racing within her natural prominent style, making the STYLE_FIT flag a modest discount rather than a dealbreaker given she genuinely leads rather than chases.
runners_data.comment: Miss Rainbow was a winner two starts back but has since disappointed with an eighth last time out, giving her a mixed profile; she has run over today's trip and going, returns after 22 days, and carries 138 lb from stall three.

runners_data.name: Methgal
runners_data.note: Prominent-running 4yo for PJ McDonald, returned nine days ago and wore tongue-tie and blinkers in recent form; 1W2P from seven runs on Good ground and produced a win over this exact trip on Good last time out — ideal profile to stalk Miss Rainbow and challenge late.
runners_data.comment: Methgal arrives on the back of a win two starts back and a runner-up finish last time out, shaped like a horse in excellent heart; he has experience of today's trip and going, and his 9-day turnaround looks sharp enough, though his sole risk may be conceding weight at 138 lb.

runners_data.name: Taygar
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with remarkable record of 14 runs from 15 on Good going, placing five times without a win; Michael Dods sends him in decent form but the controlled gallop gives him little late petrol to deploy off a true closer's tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Taygar has placed twice in her last six starts, and having run over today's trip and going, she arrives with relevant experience and a fitness edge at just 17 days since her last outing; the concern is that she has been winless in recent starts and must shoulder 137 lb from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Ottawa
runners_data.note: Liam Bailey runner with no wins or places across 15 runs on Soft-biased ground, and all five recent history runs came on Standish — the shift to Good is an unknown; his natural tendency is to come from well off the pace, though the field's composition forces him into a less authentic mid-race position, compounding an already difficult profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Ottawa faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and returns after 19 days, but consecutive unplaced efforts make him hard to fancy at 134 lb from stall ten.

runners_data.name: Neapolitan
runners_data.note: 311 days off the track for Antony Brittain is a significant red flag; has placed five times but entirely on Soft-biased ground and this Good surface represents a meaningful concern — his true running style is late and deep, but the pace shape here offers him little opportunity to express it from wherever he actually settles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 311 days off, Neapolitan faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 62 offers a sliver of encouragement from stall six carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby saddles a 3yo prominent racer who has run 14 times on Good or similar, winning once; David Allan rides and the horse's recent form includes a win over 6f on Good — tracking the pace is natural to him and he is a credible threat to Miss Rainbow if the gallop is conservative.
runners_data.comment: Hares Bredth shaped well enough last time with a third, but the overall profile is patchy, and ranked seventh of nine on our figures he faces a stiff task; the win in his last six starts came four starts back, and he has since slipped back into modest form.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Jason Hart partners a lightly raced 3yo for Rebecca Menzies with an excellent Good-ground record — 2W6P from 14 runs; has won twice over 6f on Good and naturally races prominently, making her a structurally sound profile for this pace shape and one of the more interesting form angles in the race.
runners_data.comment: Battenburg Belle arrives here in fair nick — a winner last time out and third two starts back — but ranked bottom of the field on our figures, making her a very tough sell despite the experience over today's trip and distance.

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: Rowan Scott rides this Liam Bailey-trained 4yo whose recent form includes multiple placed efforts on Good ground; naturally a hold-up type who cannot get his preferred position in this field's configuration, meaning his 0W3P in similar conditions flatters him slightly and his chance hinges on a chaotic pace scenario that looks unlikely.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Rainbow is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride into an uncontested position from the gates and dictate a sustainable gallop around Catterick's flat six furlongs. Methgal and Hares Bredth are the natural prominent horses who will press into second and third, but neither is a front-runner, so Miss Rainbow retains the initiative without being truly pressured into suicidal fractions. The field holds more hold-up types than can authentically operate from the rear — Ottawa, Neapolitan, and Wait For It are genuine closers redistributed to midfield on the map because Daytona Lady, Giant, and Taygar will occupy the genuine back positions, meaning those three redistibuted horses cannot execute their true waiting tactics and face a compromised race shape. A controlled, single-paced gallop set by Miss Rainbow on Good ground favours prominent racers who can track the leader and pounce in the final furlong — those who travel in the first three are structurally best placed, while authentic hold-up horses face a test of raw ability rather than tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Rainbow Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow secures an uncontested lead and sets an honest but manageable gallop, allowing her to dictate every yard.
scenarios.body: She dictates the fractions from her prominent draw, never truly challenged, and the field strings out behind without the closing burst needed to reel her in on Good ground over six furlongs at Catterick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow's uncontested lead causes her to go off too conservatively, leaving prominent-tracking types to collar her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Methgal and Battenburg Belle, tucking into positions two and three, apply pressure turning for home and their sustained momentum proves too much for the leader in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entering the final two furlongs and a gap opens wide enough for a genuine closer to thread through.
scenarios.body: Giant, who holds strong recent form on Good going including a win, would be the chief beneficiary of any dramatic late fade by the leaders, as would Taygar who has consistent placed form on this surface.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Break, Pack Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the start is messy and multiple runners break sharply, disrupting Miss Rainbow's uncontested lead and compressing the field into a bunch finish.
scenarios.body: A scrambled pace scenario throws the race open to whoever finds the cleanest passage, with Hares Bredth and Battenburg Belle best positioned by profile to benefit from mid-race congestion.

watchPoints.text: Miss Rainbow — if she quickens clear turning for home without any rider pressing her, the race may be effectively over early; watch whether Connor Beasley dictates or settles, as that choice defines every other runner's fate.

Methgal and Hares Bredth — both are natural prominent types who will compete for the position directly behind Miss Rainbow; if they bump or cover each other turning in, the winner of that duel between them becomes the most dangerous rival to the leader.

Battenburg Belle — has the best Good-ground profile among the prominent types after Miss Rainbow and could be underestimated if her 3yo weight advantage at the bottom of the weights allows Jason Hart to travel smoothly throughout.

Ottawa and Neapolitan — both are genuine hold-up horses pressed into a midfield shape they cannot naturally exploit; if either makes an unexpected move to go forward from the gate, it would fundamentally change the race's tempo and warrant reassessment of the lead scenario.

Giant — his most recent run was a 6f Good-ground win and he is the most credible beneficiary if the pace completely collapses, but watch whether Clifford Lee chooses to position him more prominently than his usual style given the compressed mid-pack.

races.name: Fifth Regiment Royal Artillery Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Kings Merchant
runners_data.note: A confirmed hold-up horse who won over seven furlongs on good ground recently for Philip Kirby and Kevin Stott; sim-going stats of 11/15 are solid, the drop back to six furlongs suits his sharp finishing style, and 38 days since last run is a comfortable return.|
runners_data.comment: Kings Merchant showed his best when winning three starts back, and he arrives here fresh after 38 days off the track with experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 139 lb from stall 2, recent efforts of fourth and fifth suggest he needs to find more.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who has won over five furlongs on good going for W H Harrison, but stepping up to six furlongs here is an unknown stretch; the five-furlong specialist profile is a concern in this trip context, and Barry McHugh needs to find a gap through a crowded rear bunch.|
runners_data.comment: Hi Lord ran third two starts back and has experience of today's distance and going, while his 69 rating underlines him as a leading threat from stall 7 at 139 lb; the risk is that he was unplaced last time out.

runners_data.name: Dream Deal
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner, travelling on a quick 9-day turnaround for Easterby and Allan with a headgear change noted (tb); his natural style — leading from the front — is perfectly matched to a field with no rival willing to take him on, and recent form shows consistency if not dominance.|
runners_data.comment: Dream Deal has run over today's trip and going but arrives winless in his last six starts, with a pair of seconds the highlight before a recent slide to seventh; the nine-day turnaround keeps him fresh, though 138 lb from stall eight is no light ask for a horse rated 62 officially.

runners_data.name: Winter Crown
runners_data.note: A 247-day absence is a significant flag here; all recent form is on standard artificial surfaces rather than turf, and the good-ground sim stats of 0W0P underline that Liam Bailey's runner is an unknown quantity returning from a long layoff — the lack of turf-going form is a real concern.|
runners_data.comment: Winter Crown won five starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating just edges him to the head of the field — but a 247-day absence and a run of unplaced efforts in recent starts make fitness the key risk.

runners_data.name: Pit Boss
runners_data.note: Legitimate prominent racer who has been placed in five of his last five starts including two wins on artificial; returning to turf after Southwell runs is the key question, but Billy Garritty keeps him close to the pace where this race shape can reward him.|
runners_data.comment: Pit Boss has run over today's trip and going, and shaped with credit in recent starts — third last time out and a winner two starts back — but 165 days off the track is a significant query, and 137 lb is a stern weight to shoulder on a comeback.

runners_data.name: Ideal Guest
runners_data.note: Harriet Bethell's seven-year-old has genuine hold-up form including a win over six furlongs on good going, but with five or more closers all heading rearward together the congestion risk is acute — the style-fit discount applies because he simply cannot get the space he needs to produce his best.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures and carrying 135 lb, Ideal Guest is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back; he was fifth last time out after 48 days off, and though he has run over today's trip and going before, the weight and low rating make him a tough sell.

runners_data.name: Solar Cooper
runners_data.note: A three-year-old whose best form came when winning over six furlongs on good ground for Mark Walford, but his natural instinct to race handy is compromised in a field where the hold-up group is so crowded; the redistribution note reflects that Oisin Orr will have company he didn't bargain for behind him.|
runners_data.comment: Solar Cooper won from this mark four starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving him a solid platform to threaten; the concern is that his last three outings have all produced finishes of sixth or worse.

runners_data.name: One Of Our Own
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's six-year-old has won over six furlongs on good ground and his sim-going stats are encouraging, but with several genuine closers mapping into the same position the straightforward late run his style demands becomes dependent on the field fanning wide — his true profile is better than his map position reflects, though the traffic problem is real.|

runners_data.name: Eldeyaar
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's veteran wears a visor and has placed form over six furlongs on good ground, but sim-going stats of just 5/15 are the worst in the field and he has struggled to replicate his one win on these conditions regularly; being shuffled into a bunched midfield group makes him a low-percentage hope.|
runners_data.comment: Eldeyaar has shown only glimpses of form in recent starts, finishing third twice and winning once in his last six, but a fifth and eighth since suggest he is struggling for consistency, and ranked ninth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Tagged with a tendency to fade in the finish, this four-year-old is on a quick five-day turnaround for Brian Rothwell with Shay Farmer claiming 5lbs; the style-fit and finishing concern combine to make her the most cautious prospect in the field, and good ground does nothing to improve her finishing record.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Aurora's Doublesix faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a light weight of 122 lb from stall three offers a crumb of comfort.

races.paceDynamic: Dream Deal is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 10-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace rival to push him along — he should stride into a clear lead from the off and control tempo on good ground over Catterick's flat six furlongs. The note that this field carries far more hold-up horses than the track can accommodate is significant: Solar Cooper, Ideal Guest, One Of Our Own, Eldeyaar, and Aurora's Doublesix are all true closers redistributed into midfield on the map, meaning the rear of the field will be congested and their ability to find clear daylight late is genuinely compromised. With Dream Deal setting a sustainable, controlled tempo unchallenged up front, the race shape heavily favours either the horse in front or the one horse who can track him closely — Kings Merchant and Pit Boss, the legitimate hold-up and prominent types with credible form, are best placed to exploit that shape. This is a pace-setter's race or a race for the nearest pursuer; hold-up horses firing late from a crowded pack face the least favourable scenario of all.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dream Deal Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal is allowed to bowl along in front at a controlled clip with no rival willing or able to close him down early.
scenarios.body: Dream Deal, racing fresh off a 9-day turnaround for Tim Easterby and David Allan, dictates from flag to finish on a flat, fair surface that rewards relaxed front-runners; good ground at Catterick's six furlongs offers no natural sapping feature to stop him. Pit Boss, tracking from a genuine prominent position, is the horse most likely to pick up the pieces if Dream Deal fades, but the map strongly suggests he holds on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal sets a pace fractionally too quick and a close-tracking prominent type collars him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Pit Boss has been placed consistently over six and seven furlongs on artificial surfaces and his first run back on turf gives cause for curiosity, but his style — legitimately prominent — means he is positioned to pounce without fighting traffic. Kings Merchant, a genuine hold-up horse with good-ground form including a recent win over this trip, could also get there from just off the pace if the front two tire together.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Split Through
scenarios.trigger: If Dream Deal's pace is genuinely fast early and the field spreads wide enough in the straight to give hold-up horses a run through.
scenarios.body: One Of Our Own and Ideal Guest both have winning form over six furlongs on good ground and carry the most credible closing profiles in the field, though both are redistributed in the map meaning they face a real risk of meeting a wall of horses. Good ground at Catterick does allow a late run down the straight if gaps appear, but the sheer number of hold-up types racing together makes this a crowded lottery.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or splits unpredictably and a lower-rated horse catches a chaotic finish at a big price.
scenarios.body: Aurora's Doublesix and Eldeyaar are the longest-priced hold-up types in the field and would only feature in a scenario where the race falls completely apart — both carry form concerns and the fade warning on Aurora's Doublesix further reduces the likelihood. This scenario exists mainly because ten runners in a compressed, slow-pace situation can occasionally produce a surprise, not because the form of these horses merits serious consideration.

watchPoints.text: Dream Deal — if David Allan gets a clean break from the stalls and immediately establishes a lead, there is no horse positioned or willing to challenge him early; watch whether any prominent horse makes an aggressive move to his outside in the first two furlongs, because if none do the race could be over as a contest by halfway.

The rear bunch — Solar Cooper, Ideal Guest, One Of Our Own, Eldeyaar, and Aurora's Doublesix are all genuine hold-up horses racing into the same quarter of the track; watch how wide they fan in the straight because if they are forced to race in a line they will impede each other's runs.

Winter Crown — 247 days off the track and a switch back to turf from artificial surfaces is a meaningful risk flag; watch market moves close to post time as any significant gamble on this horse would suggest stable confidence that outsiders cannot assess from the form book alone.

Pit Boss — his five consecutive placed efforts on artificial surfaces suggest he is reliable and consistent, but watch whether Billy Garritty positions him close to Dream Deal from the outset rather than allowing a gap to open, as that tracking position is the key to whether he can get to the front-runner.

Kings Merchant — Kevin Stott's record on this horse and the recent seven-furlong win on good going make him the hold-up horse with the most straightforward profile; watch his draw and whether he can find a clear run down the outside of the straight rather than getting caught behind the cluster of closers.

races.name: Every Race Live On Racing Tv Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Taaklam
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race; Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claimer) rides for in-form Harriet Bethell (2 from 7 in 14 days) and with just 8 days since its last run the horse is fresh, but its recent form figures of 325761 show inconsistency and its similar-going record is modest (0W0P from 3 attempts on comparable ground).
runners_data.comment: Taaklam arrives here on the back of a win last time out, and at just eight days' freshness he looks in fine order to go again; he has run over today's trip and going before, and his 141 lb burden is the one thing to manage.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is firing at 12/41 in the last fortnight, but this hold-up specialist has posted five consecutive fifth-or-worse finishes including three on Good ground at 7f, and Sam James will face a significant task navigating traffic from the rear in a compressed field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and beaten into eighth last time out just four days ago, Light The Night Up does at least have experience over today's trip and going, and her trainer's 29% strike rate over the past fortnight offers some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Real Jack
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners a horse that has finished sixth or seventh in its last four starts and its similar-going record at 7f on Good is unremarkable (0W0P); 32 days since last run is not alarming but the form string offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest among the 12 runners here and carrying 134 lb from stall six, Real Jack brings experience over today's trip and going and returns after 32 days off; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts, and his recent finishing positions offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Kilmac Air
runners_data.note: Jason Hart rides, and the horse's best effort this season came at 7f on Heavy; it is a genuine closer by nature, though the field's density pushes it into a midfield slot it does not naturally want — any chance depends on getting a clear run late that this race shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: Kilmac Air shaped with promise when third three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going counts in her favour, with a rating of 67 suggesting she retains more ability than her official mark implies; the risk is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Territorial Star
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies sends this one out after a 105-day absence, and while the horse has shown ability at this trip (two placed efforts over 7f on Soft), the long layoff combined with a hold-up style in a slow-paced race makes it difficult to be bullish; tongue-tie fitted.
runners_data.comment: Territorial Star has experience over today's trip and shaped with promise when third in her last five starts — yet to score in recent outings — but 105 days off the track is the key risk heading into this.

runners_data.name: Maynora
runners_data.note: Clifford Lee rides for Craig Lidster (1/7 in 14 days) and the horse's last-six form includes a win over 6f on Soft and multiple placed efforts on Good; its similar-going record is the strongest in the field (8/15 runs with 0W1P) and it showed tactical versatility with a second over 6f on Good recently, giving it an each-way profile.
runners_data.comment: Maynora won one start back five runs ago but has since posted a second last time out amid a run of mid-pack finishes, and 64 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 65 suggests some ability to exploit.

runners_data.name: Willowinghurn
runners_data.note: David Tudhope takes the ride for David O'Meara (4/46 in 14 days, a modest strike rate) and this horse's natural habitat is at the rear of the field over 7-8f; its form cycle has been inconsistent (056838) but it has placed four times over similar trips on Good ground, though it cannot get its preferred position in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Willowinghurn is yet to win in her last six starts, though a third two runs back offers a flicker of hope; she has run over today's trip and going before, and draws stall one carrying 130 lb, but a return to eighth last time out is the concern.

runners_data.name: Singarda
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood share training duties; this horse races in a tongue-tie and blinkers combination and has been placed twice over 8f on Good going, but stepping down to 7f is a query and, as a true hold-up type pushed toward midfield by the race's shape, it will struggle to exploit its natural finishing style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, Singarda makes little appeal despite the experience over today's trip and going; a 33-day absence and 129 lb add further questions to a profile that is simply hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's runner has shown one bright effort — a second over 6f on Good — but its last seven runs include an eighth and a seventh, and as a hold-up horse bumped outward on the pace map it will need significant improvement from its recent form to feature; Aiden Brookes rides.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Oasis Cover does hold a second five starts back as evidence she can reach the frame, though recent efforts — including an eighth last time out — make it hard to fancy her strongly from stall four off 129 lb.

runners_data.name: Lope Y Linda
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's in-form operation (14/87 in 14 days, one of the better 14-day strike rates in this field) sends out a genuine prominent racer with a win over 6f on Soft and four placed efforts at 6-7f on Good; David Allan is an experienced northern-circuit rider and this horse is the most natural ally to Taaklam at the front end.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Lope Y Linda faces a stiff task from stall 12 carrying 128 lb, and being ranked ninth of twelve on our figures makes her hard to fancy, though she has experience over today's trip and going and comes here just eight days after finishing second.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: James Sullivan partners Lanarra for R Mike Smith (2/9 in 14 days) and this is probably the most encouraging form of the hold-up contingent — a recent win over 7f on Good and placed at 6f on both Good and Soft suggests the horse handles these conditions well; the problem is getting a clear run from a congested midfield group in a slowly-run race.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Lanarra is hard to fancy at the weights, though her win last time out at least brings some recent form to the table; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 13 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Belling The Cat
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie rides for the Coyle & Wood yard; a blinkers-and-hold-up type, this horse has never won and its last three finishes read 4-7-8, with its best effort (fourth, 7f, Good) offering a slim angle but not enough to overcome a race shape that pushes it away from its natural rear-of-field slot.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Belling The Cat is hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround in reasonable order.

races.paceDynamic: Taaklam is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one other prominent-minded horse (Lope Y Linda) likely to push forward, the pace here figures to be steady and uncontested — a single horse controlling the tempo from the front at Catterick's 7f with no genuine rival to pressurise it. Lope Y Linda may attempt to sit a length or two off the leader but is unlikely to force Taaklam into anything uncomfortable, meaning the early fractions on Good ground should be measured rather than searching. The remainder of the field — Maynora, Light The Night Up, Real Jack, and the redistributed hold-up brigade — will be stacked through midfield and towards the rear, creating a tight, compressed bunch behind the leader. This shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than true closers, because a steady early pace will not create enough of a tempo-induced gap for late finishers to exploit; notably, Kilmac Air, Willowinghurn, Singarda, Oasis Cover, Lanarra, and Belling The Cat are all genuine hold-up types that cannot realistically get their natural position in this field, reducing the closing threat and further entrenching the advantage for front-end and prominent racing profiles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Taaklam Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Taaklam is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured pace and the hold-up pack fails to generate sufficient momentum from the rear.
scenarios.body: Taaklam sets a comfortable rhythm on Good turf and simply never faces a serious challenge, with Lope Y Linda tracking but unable to quicken past; the compressed field behind cannot accelerate quickly enough over the final furlong because the tempo never truly wound up to test the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Fight Out Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda tracks Taaklam closely and the pair kick turning for home, leaving the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: Lope Y Linda, carrying Tim Easterby's recent 14/87 in-form send-out record, has the experience and prominent style to match strides with Taaklam over the final two furlongs; the steady gallop means the closers never generate the late surge needed to collar them, and the race is settled between the front two.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If Lope Y Linda does push Taaklam harder than expected in the early stages, lifting the pace enough to stretch the field and open a lane for one hold-up horse to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: A marginally stronger gallop would leave Taaklam vulnerable at the death and one of the genuine closers — Maynora or Lanarra, both of whom have proven form at this trip on Good ground — could pick up the pieces with a well-timed run through the middle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Taaklam sets an even slower crawl than anticipated, causing the entire field to bunch and the winner to emerge from midfield off a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: With a near-stationary early gallop the race degenerates into a sprint in the final 2f, suiting any horse agile enough to find a gap quickly; Maynora and Territorial Star, both capable of a sharp finishing effort at this trip, are best placed to benefit from chaos in a bunched field.

watchPoints.text: Taaklam is the only horse with a clear lead over the field — watch for whether Tom Kiely-Marshall attempts to dictate from the front immediately, as any cover or early pressure from Lope Y Linda could fundamentally alter the pace shape.

Lope Y Linda's position in the early stages is critical: if David Allan elects to push forward aggressively and sit directly on Taaklam's shoulder rather than tracking at a length, the pace will quicken materially and closers such as Maynora and Lanarra could benefit.

With six horses tagged as redistributed hold-up types crowding midfield, there is a heightened risk of significant traffic problems entering the straight — runners like Kilmac Air, Singarda, and Oasis Cover will all be seeking gaps simultaneously in a tightly packed field.

Territorial Star's 105-day layoff for Rebecca Menzies warrants monitoring in the market and in the paddock; a well-prepared reappearance over a trip it has shown ability at could represent more than its current profile suggests, particularly if the pace is steady and the ground suits.

Lanarra's recent 7f Good win gives it the most relevant recent form of the hold-up horses — watch whether James Sullivan manages to find a position closer to midfield than the furthest rear, as even a half-length of ground saved could prove decisive if the closers do get their run.

races.name: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with strong recent form (1W, 2nd twice in last five), goes well on Good ground with 7/12 sim-going record including a win; Zak Wheatley rides and 35 days since last run is fine — this trip and surface suits.
runners_data.comment: Captain Cess shaped with real promise when runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back gives him solid recent form to build on; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 35 days between runs leaves him fresh to go again.

runners_data.name: Showtime Mahomes
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type whose sim-going record on Good is poor (0 wins, 0 places from 4 runs); Sam James rides but the form figures on this surface (11th last time on Good) give little confidence.
runners_data.comment: Showtime Mahomes holds the highest rating in this field and his win in his last six starts shows he can deliver when the conditions are right; he has run over today's trip and going before, but his two unplaced efforts in recent starts are the concern at 134 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Saisons d'Or
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race; 11-year-old who won over 7f on Standard and placed three times on Good — Jack Garritty can control tempo freely; sole pacesetter status is the defining tactical asset here, though age and a modest recent string are caveats.
runners_data.comment: Saisons d'Or won five starts back and has experience of both today's trip and going, so the conditions hold no terrors, while his rating of 63 ranks him third of these eleven; the concern is two sevenths in his last three starts that suggests he may be out of form.

runners_data.name: Secret Road
runners_data.note: Prominent type dropping back to 7f from 8f and further; has headgear noted and T14 of 1/1 is an encouraging trainer strike rate, but recent form on Tapeta suggests course-form confirmation is needed and this trip is on the sharp end.

runners_data.name: Jenni
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with decent Good-ground form (wins and places in sim-going), returns after 47 days; David Nolan is an experienced northern jockey who knows Catterick, but the 10th and 9th on this trip last season need addressing before confidence is high.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and yet to recapture the fourth she managed two runs back, Jenni does have experience of today's trip and conditions in her favour, though 47 days off the track and 132 lb to carry leave her with plenty to prove from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Filey Beach
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with three wins and three places from 15 sim-going runs; only 10 days since last run, which is sharp turnaround, but Ruth Carr trains them fit and the horse has placed four times in its last five starts over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Ranked tenth of eleven on our figures and representing a trainer who has sent out just one winner from 28 runners in the past fortnight, Filey Beach makes this hard work, despite drawing stall one, experience over today's trip and going, and a winning run six starts back.

runners_data.name: Electric Lightning
runners_data.note: Prominent runner stepping down from 8f to 7f; placed twice on Good at 8f recently, so the trip shortening is a question — the switch could sharpen or unsettle; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a small help on OR=56.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Electric Lightning at least brings distance and going experience to the table, and a second two starts back hints at some residual ability — though 52 days off the track and a relatively modest official rating of 56 leave questions to answer here.

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: Strong recent form includes two places on Good over today's course and distance range; however, this natural hold-up performer is pushed into a midfield berth by the crowded rear contingent, meaning she won't get her cleanest run — form is solid but positional compromise is real.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Miss Willows faces a stiff task here; a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, but fourth last time out and an official mark of 56 make her hard to fancy despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Maui Breeze
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who prefers to come from off the pace (hg:p noted), but similarly displaced into midfield by the number of hold-up types; 66 days off the track adds a fitness query and the 0W0P sim-going record makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and absent for 66 days, Maui Breeze faces a stiff task from stall 10 carrying 128 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a rating of 60 offers some encouragement for a midfield shout.

runners_data.name: She's A Goldigger
runners_data.note: Placed three times recently on varied surfaces; a true closer who will be racing towards the middle of the pack rather than from the rear where she is most effective — the style mismatch is a genuine handicap, and 74 days off adds to the uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, She's A Goldigger faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a third two starts back shows she can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent type with four consecutive fourth-place finishes, suggesting consistent but limited form; Rowan Scott rides and OR=46 gives plenty of weight advantage; Catterick 7f Good is well within scope and consistency could see him involved late without threatening the principals.
runners_data.comment: Mister Sky Blue shaped with plenty of promise when third three starts back, and he returns fresh enough at 13 days since his last run, having run over today's trip and going; our rating of 60 puts him firmly in contention, though the trainer's current 5% strike rate is the chief concern.

races.paceDynamic: Saisons d'Or is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f Catterick handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jack Garritty should be able to dictate a controlled, honest gallop on Good ground rather than an injurious burn-up. Secret Road, Filey Beach, Electric Lightning, and Mister Sky Blue will push forward to dispute the prominent positions, creating a competitive but not chaotic early order that keeps the pace honest without overcooking it. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate cleanly — Miss Willows, Maui Breeze, and She's A Goldigger are true closers who are likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield rather than their preferred deep rear berth, which materially reduces their ability to produce a late surge. This controlled single-pace setup with a compact prominent group travelling sweetly into the final two furlongs strongly favours prominent and handy racers who can strike from a position of comfort without needing a strong injection of pace from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saisons d'Or Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Saisons d'Or leads at a steady-to-honest clip and the prominent group travels within themselves into the straight.
scenarios.body: Saisons d'Or sets a measured tempo, allowing the prominent horses to cover off any late challengers without being exposed; on Good ground at Catterick, those closest to the pace over 7f are hardest to pass.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Front Runner Steals
scenarios.trigger: If Saisons d'Or is permitted to go even slower than expected and no rival is willing to press.
scenarios.body: The pace becomes truly false, rewarding the horse in front who bowls along in a comfort zone and simply outstays rivals who cannot quicken from cold; Saisons d'Or's previous win at 7f on Standard gives some evidence it can finish strongly when fresh.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Thread Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and create clear gaps for late runners to exploit.
scenarios.body: A genuinely strong tempo benefits horses closing from the rear, but Miss Willows, Maui Breeze, and She's A Goldigger are all displaced from their natural positions by the crowded hold-up contingent, making a clean late run harder to engineer; Captain Cess is the most plausible beneficiary as a genuine hold-up type with good form on this going.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Race, Congestion Favours Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for prominent spots creates traffic chaos and a non-fancied runner benefits from a clear run.
scenarios.body: With four horses chasing early positions behind Saisons d'Or, a rough passage is possible; a lightly-weighted runner like Mister Sky Blue or She's A Goldigger could capitalise if rivals interfere with each other.

watchPoints.text: Saisons d'Or's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the race's pivotal factor — if anything pressures Jack Garritty early, the race shape changes entirely and prominent horses like Filey Beach become even more dangerous.

The cluster of Secret Road, Electric Lightning, Filey Beach, and Mister Sky Blue all wanting prominent positions could cause jostling in the first two furlongs; watch for any of them losing ground or getting shuffled back at the start.

Miss Willows has genuine Good-ground form but will need a clean run from a compromised midfield position — Connor Beasley will need to find a gap early in the straight for her finishing effort to count.
Filey Beach's 10-day turnaround is the shortest in the field; Ruth Carr does run horses fit back-to-back, but monitor market moves for any sign of confidence or concern from connections.

Captain Cess is the hold-up runner with the most credible recent Good-ground form and comes in fresh at 35 days — if pace is honest enough to string the field, he is the most natural beneficiary of a closing run.

races.name: Rmg Proudly Supports Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with two wins at 5f on Good going in recent form — Tristan Davidson's string is in a T14 purple patch (5/12) and Jason Hart rides a horse who travels prominently and handles today's conditions well; the 8-day turnaround from a winning run is a mild concern but he showed resilience last time.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner three starts back, Our Absent Friends arrives fresh on eight days' rest with distance and going experience in his favour; the main risk is a weight of 138 lb from stall seven.

runners_data.name: Military Girl
runners_data.note: Michael Dods has a T14 return of only 2/30, but Connor Beasley partners a mare who has won twice on Good going over 5f and finished second in between — her 12/15 similar-going record is outstanding, and she will try to lock onto a prominent pitch from the off.|
runners_data.comment: Ran well to finish second three starts back and has won twice in her last six, but her last two outings have yielded a fifth and an unplaced effort, suggesting she heads here in a dip in form; has run over today's trip and going, and 136 lb is the notable weight burden to overcome from stall six.

runners_data.name: J Street
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with wins at 5f on Good and Standard, making up a prominent trio for the Easterby team; the 32-day break is the main query, but the 7/15 similar-going record and two wins in recent history suggest she is fit enough to be competitive racing near the pace.|
runners_data.comment: A run of back-to-back fourths in her most recent starts makes J Street hard to fancy, ranked seventh of nine on our figures, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her two wins in her last six starts confirm she is capable of better.

runners_data.name: I'm Dan Dare
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who wears a hood (p) and has won over today's course and distance on Good ground — the 60-day layoff is notable, but Mark Walford's T14 return of 1/13 is modest and the headgear change gives him a potential edge if freshness translates to early sharpness from a prominent position.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of nine on our figures and with a speed rating of 67 that leaves him plenty to find, I'm Dan Dare is hard to fancy despite a record showing two wins in his last six starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 60 days off adds another question mark.

runners_data.name: Hanney Girl
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field and wears a tongue-tie (t) for Tim Easterby, who sends out 14 from 87 over the past fortnight — David Allan can dictate on the front end without pressure, but the mare's recent form shows three nines in five starts and her ability to hold on once challenged at 5f on Good ground is unproven at her best.|
runners_data.comment: Hanney Girl carries a hefty 134 lb from stall five, yet her rating of 84 marks her out as the standout in this field, and she has run over today's trip and conditions before; the concern is that she has been winless in her last six starts, with consecutive fourths in recent outings suggesting the win may continue to elude her.

runners_data.name: Wen Moon
runners_data.note: Aiden Brookes partners a genuine hold-up type who has finished in the frame twice at 5f on Good going and is returning from 97 days off — the lengthy absence is a significant concern, though Ben Haslam's T14 strike rate of 4/19 suggests the yard is not out of form, and this horse's natural style makes him the most authentic closer in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last two starts, Wen Moon lines up here fresh after 97 days off, but his recent consistency is the key, and he has experience over today's distance and going; carrying 134 lb from stall one, our figures suggest he holds strong claims.

runners_data.name: Valor Spirit
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart's three-year-old has placed twice at 6f on Good but is positioned at the rear of the map despite being a natural prominent racer — his 0/8 T14 blank for the trainer tempers enthusiasm, and racing genuinely out of his preferred role reduces his realistic chance considerably.|
runners_data.comment: Valor Spirit has shown a knack for placing, with a second last time out and a second three starts back, though a sixth two starts back tempers enthusiasm; yet to win in recent starts, and 52 days between runs is a query, even if today's trip and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Keldeo
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears runner has placed second at 5f on Good and carries good course profile, but his natural inclination to race prominently cannot be satisfied in a field this congested up front — Harry Russell will need to find a gap from an unnatural midfield berth, which the horse's style profile suggests he will find difficult.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Keldeo is hard to fancy despite a recent second three starts back keeping hope faint; experience over today's trip and going, plus a 22-day freshen-up, are the slim positives from stall three off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Protest Rally
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope partners a horse returning after 396 days off — an enormous absence that is the single largest flag in the race — and despite an exceptional 15/15 similar-going record built over previous campaigns, expecting a true-to-form run first time back after over a year away is a significant ask regardless of his natural prominent style being compromised here.|
runners_data.comment: Protest Rally showed enough in his last five starts to catch the eye, and his experience over today's trip and conditions is a genuine asset; carrying 131 lb from stall nine and returning after 396 days off is the chief concern for this winless gelding.

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman (3lb claim) rides for Tina Jackson, whose T14 return is a blank (0/3); at OR 56 this runner meets horses rated up to 18lb superior, and although winning at 5f on Good last time, her positional displacement from a natural prominent style into mapped midfield compounds an already-testing assignment at the weights.|

races.paceDynamic: Hanney Girl is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Allan can dictate terms from the front at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over this sharp Catterick 5f. However, there is significant congestion behind her: Our Absent Friends, Military Girl, J Street, and I'm Dan Dare all want to race prominently, creating a scramble for the first three positions that will generate interference and traffic danger between the 2f and 3f markers. Keldeo, Protest Rally, and Without Flaw are natural prominent racers who cannot all get their preferred berth and will be shuffled back into midfield roles that suit them less well, meaning the hold-up section of this field is artificially inflated by horses racing out of character. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel fluidly just off the leader's shoulder — true prominent types with the tactical speed to slot in behind Hanney Girl and benefit from a controlled pace — rather than deep closers who will face a wall of horses with no natural daylight opening up late. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their desired position; Our Absent Friends, Military Girl, and I'm Dan Dare are best-placed to actually land prominent berths given their style, age, and recent form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hanney Girl Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hanney Girl leads uncontested and the prominent group settles cleanly into position behind her, allowing the race to develop at a true but manageable pace.
scenarios.body: Hanney Girl sets honest fractions without being pressured, and the horses travelling just off the pace have the ideal platform to challenge in the final furlong on this flat, undemanding track; the pace is honest enough to find out horses with stamina questions but not so severe that the leader is swamped.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Aids Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the congestion behind Hanney Girl causes bumping and checking, she steals an unassailable lead while rivals behind cancel each other out.
scenarios.body: The jostling for the three or four prominent spots burns energy and creates traffic chaos for the horses racing slightly wide or squeezed on the rail, and Hanney Girl simply extends her advantage without a serious challenge reaching her; this scenario suits horses who can lead or race closest to the pace with a clear run rather than those forced widest to avoid trouble.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong due to multiple horses pressing Hanney Girl harder than expected, creating a true test of stamina that sees the lead group weaken.
scenarios.body: An honest gallop stretches the field and opens a gap on the rail in the final furlong for horses who have settled conservatively; Wen Moon, who holds a genuine hold-up profile and has good recent form at 5f on Good ground, is best-placed among the true closers to finish strongly if this scenario unfolds.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Hanney Girl leads at a very slow tempo and no horse is willing to challenge, causing the whole field to bunch and produce a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: A sprint-finish lottery favours horses with the most raw speed and cleanest run; redistributed prominent types like Keldeo or Protest Rally, despite racing out of role, would benefit if they happen to find daylight at the critical moment, though their chances here are inherently discounted given their unnatural positioning.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion — Our Absent Friends, Military Girl, J Street, and I'm Dan Dare will all be fighting for the same two or three positions behind Hanney Girl in the first furlong, creating a high risk of bumping and interference that could end the race for at least one of them early.

Protest Rally's 396-day absence is the most extreme layoff in the field — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the paddock and early in the race, as even a fit returner would find it hard to reproduce career form from this blank, and Tudhope may be instructed simply to give the horse a confidence run.

Hanney Girl's recent form string of 539944 conceals a front-runner who has not finished in the top three in her last three attempts on Good ground — if the pace she sets is softer than it appears, she may simply be swamped in the final furlong rather than rewarded for controlled front-running.

Wen Moon returns from 97 days off and is the only genuine hold-up runner in the field — watch how he moves through the field at the 2f pole; if the pace has been honest, he is the most natural beneficiary of a strongly-run race, but the layoff means fitness is unconfirmed.|

I'm Dan Dare switches to headgear (hood) today after winning at this course over this trip — hood-first runs can produce a marked behavioural change, and Jack Garritty will need to manage any exuberance early from a horse who already wants to race prominently in a congested field.|

races.name: Racing Again 30th September Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Zimmerman
runners_data.note: Consistent stayer with recent wins at 14f and 16f, trainer Tim Easterby in good 14-day form (14/87), and wearing tongue strap; a true hold-up horse repositioned to a midfield slot on the pace map as the field is saturated with closers, which tempers his chance if the gallop is steady and traffic is dense.
runners_data.comment: Zimmerman arrives on the back of consecutive wins and is fitter than most coming here just four days on, with experience over today's trip and conditions lending further confidence; the 157 lb burden is the one query, but his recent form is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Pedro The Poet
runners_data.note: Nicky Richards sends him here in good yard form (1/2 in 14 days) but his recent form is modest and his distance history is well short of this 1m6f trip, with runs largely over 8f-10f — a stamina question mark hangs over him on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Pedro The Poet arrives here on the back of a tough recent spell, winless in his last six starts, yet our rating has him narrowly at the head of this field and he returns on a quick turnaround just 12 days since his last outing with going experience in his favour; the chief concern is that his official mark of 64 and 156 lb in the weights make a first success elusive.

runners_data.name: Good Onya Mate
runners_data.note: Michael Bell-trained four-year-old with a consistent form string at this sort of trip, including two fourths at 16f on Good — wears a hood and has shown enough to suggest he stays, though his inability to win in nine attempts at this trip is a concern; a natural hold-up horse likely in the thick of the midfield pack.
runners_data.comment: Good Onya Mate is yet to win in his last six starts, though a second four starts back and two consecutive fourths in recent outings suggest he is knocking at the door; carrying 156 lb under his official mark of 64 may be the stiffest obstacle here.

runners_data.name: Chambers
runners_data.note: Won last time out at 14f on Good (form: 1) having also scored at 14f previously, giving him solid course-and-distance credentials for a stayer; jockey Mr James Hills claims 5lb and trainer Faye Bramley has a 1/9 14-day strike rate, but the 39-day absence is worth noting — his profile suits a steadily-run race where he can track and pick off tiring rivals.

runners_data.name: Star Start
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for this race, Ruth Carr's six-year-old has an excellent recent record of wins and places (321221) and goes fresh on a five-day turnaround; she sets the entire complexion of this race and her ability to dictate a controllable gallop unchallenged is the single most important tactical factor — her STYLE_FIT tag notes she is tagged as Prominent rather than Lead, so the lone-front-running role is slightly outside her typical operating zone.
runners_data.comment: Rated bottom of the pile on our figures and carrying a hefty 154 lb, Star Start is hard to fancy despite a trainer badly out of form at 1/28 over the past fortnight; in his favour, he has winning form in his last six starts and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Saratoga Gold
runners_data.note: Kevin & Lauren Frost's eight-year-old has a strong record of placing on Good ground (0W5P in similar going), has finished in the first three at 12f-14f recently, and wears a hood; though his natural instinct is to race held up, the pace map places him in midfield given the volume of closers — his Good-ground consistency gives him a statistical argument, but he is technically racing out of his preferred position.
runners_data.comment: Saratoga Gold shaped well when third last time out and, carrying 153 lb with experience over today's trip and going, he rates a solid each-way threat at a rating of 68; the risk is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Nanny Park
runners_data.note: Won at 14f on Good not long ago and has placed at 12f on Good, suggesting she handles the conditions well; Sara Ender's yard has 0 from 6 in the last 14 days which is a slight negative, but her staying form and Good-ground record are genuine positives — she is a hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the pace map given the crowded rear of the field, which means a clear run is not guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Nanny Park won four starts back but has found little since, and three consecutive below-par efforts since that victory leave her with plenty to prove; she has run over today's trip and going, and at 152 lb there is a weight question too.

runners_data.name: Cougar
runners_data.note: Michael Chapman's seven-year-old has a poor recent record (0-7-5-5-7 in last five, no wins or places on Good going) and has been running over shorter trips of 11f-12f rather than this 1m6f test — the step up in trip, weak form, and trainer's 0/3 14-day record combine to make him the hardest to back; occupies a redistributed midfield slot as a genuine hold-up type in an overcrowded rear of the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Cougar faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick eight-day turnaround carrying 150 lb.

runners_data.name: Fleur de Mer
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's six-year-old wears a visor and has placed at 12f and 16f, but only 2 of 15 comparable-going runs have been on Good turf — a notable going-suitability concern; she is a hold-up horse that the map has pushed into midfield, and with the pace likely to be modest, her late run may not materialise over a trip that has seen mixed results.
runners_data.comment: Fleur de Mer has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going; the concern is that she remains yet to win in her last six outings.

races.paceDynamic: Star Start is the lone confirmed front runner in this nine-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to control the tempo from the front over this 1m6f trip on Good ground at Catterick — a sustainable, uncontested gallop that will almost certainly be steadier in the early stages than the race may appear on paper. The field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types, meaning the race will likely compress into a slowly-run affair with a bunched midfield before the pace picks up in the straight, suiting horses who can travel close enough to the action to pounce rather than those needing to make up significant ground from off the pace. This race shape favours prominent racers and those capable of travelling just behind the leader in a compact group, allowing them to kick with Star Start or go past her in the closing stages — pure closers needing a true honest gallop to use their finishing kick are at a structural disadvantage here. Several runners — Zimmerman, Saratoga Gold, Nanny Park, Cougar, and Fleur de Mer — are genuine hold-up types that the pace map has redistributed to midfield, meaning the field contains more horses needing ground to make up than this steady pace will comfortably accommodate; of those, Saratoga Gold and Nanny Park, with their Good-ground profiles and pattern of placing, are most likely to navigate the compact traffic and land closest to the action.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Star Start Dictates Steadily
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start bowls along unchallenged and sets a controlled, moderate gallop that stretches into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Star Start controls the tempo throughout, and the race turns into a tactical affair decided by which horses have tracked close enough to deliver their effort at the right moment; horses with a prominent profile and good finishing kick off a slow-run race dominate the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Navigate Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough that one of the redistributed true hold-up horses finds a clear run from off the pace and finishes strongly.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop catches out horses who sprint too early, and a horse arriving late with a clean passage finds the leaders tying up inside the final furlong; this scenario is discounted because the redistributed hold-up types are racing out of their natural position and may not secure the ground-making run they need.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Star Start Falters Late
scenarios.trigger: If Star Start's recent five-day turnaround catches up with her and she fades in the straight, allowing a prominent tracker to strike.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third throughout takes advantage as Star Start weakens from the two-furlong pole, turning a controlled tactical race into a straightforward staying test; the winner here is one who has tracked sensibly and conserved energy in the mid-race lull.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield produces interference or multiple horses hit the front simultaneously in a sprint-for-home scramble.
scenarios.body: With most of the field bunched and racing partly out of role, a messy final two furlongs produces a very tight finish where positional luck plays a large part; lower-rated runners like Cougar or Pedro The Poet could fluke a place, though a winning chance for either remains slim on ratings and form.

watchPoints.text: Star Start is the sole pace-setter and if she underperforms on her five-day turnaround, the entire race shape collapses — watch her in the parade ring for signs of freshness or tension.

With five genuinely redistributed hold-up horses — Zimmerman, Saratoga Gold, Nanny Park, Cougar, and Fleur de Mer — all compressed into the midfield, there is a significant risk of traffic problems and interference in the straight; watch for horses becoming boxed in on the approach to the home turn.

Chambers is the most live closer given his recent win on Good at 14f, but his 39-day layoff means fitness is unproven — watch how he moves through the race from the two-furlong pole as an indicator of whether the break has left him short.

Saratoga Gold and Nanny Park both have solid Good-ground placing records and are the redistributed hold-up horses most likely to secure a decent position in the midfield pack — watch their early positioning as a guide to whether they can overcome the race-shape disadvantage.

Pedro The Poet's stamina for 1m6f is entirely unproven given his recent runs over 8f-10f — watch him in the final quarter-mile for signs of distress, as a fading performance here would confirm the trip is beyond him.
